GPT-4.","source":"C12"},{"item_type":"decision","point":"D1","problem":"Which question to pursue after finding the Reversal Curse.","did":"He prioritizes the general question of which out-of-context inferences models can and cannot make over the Reversal Curse itself.","alternatives_named":["focusing on the specific Reversal Curse case"],"stated_reason":"Reversal Curse is a basic result once you explore the space of out-of-context inference, and the broader map matters for situational awareness and emergent goals.","quote":"I'm less interested in the specific case of the Reversal Curse than in the general question of what out-of-context inferences are possible and which happen in practice.","source":"C14"},{"item_type":"disagreement","point":"D6","problem":"Whether a flaw that rarely shows up in real data and benchmarks is worth caring about.","did":"He argues that facts which matter for novel research may be poorly represented in training sets, so such flaws can matter.","alternatives_named":["only care about flaws that show up in performance on benchmarks and common data"],"stated_reason":"Important facts for novel cognitive work may be recent, underrated or misunderstood, and so rare in training data.","quote":"However, if you want to use a model to do novel STEM research (or any kind of novel cognitive work), there might be facts that are important but not very well represented in training sets because they were recently discovered or are underrated or misunderstood by humans.","source":"C14"},{"item_type":"rejected","point":"D5","problem":"Whether effect than a Bayesian account would predict.","alternatives_named":["models behave close to Bayesian reasoning"],"stated_reason":"Observed effects of realized descriptions on unrealized descriptions are smaller than Bayesian reasoning would predict, and the ground truth for optimal reasoning is hard to define.","quote":"From the Bayesian perspective, including \"realized descriptions\" should have a significant impact on how much the model is influenced by \"unrealized descriptions\". The effects we see seem smaller than expected (see Figure 4 and Table 2).","source":"C19"},{"item_type":"advice","point":"D2","problem":"Introspection science seems to lack ground truth in the cases that matter most.","did":"He recommends evaluating on large, diverse datasets where ground truth exists and using them to inform harder cases.","alternatives_named":["giving up on introspection where ground truth is unavailable"],"stated_reason":"Ground truth is expensive, noisy and contentious for questions like goals or feelings, but large datasets with ground truth may transfer help to those cases.","quote":"Moreover, we can get evaluate models against very large and diverse datasets where we do have groundtruth.
